jamie: Ran nsys trace on ded-8 under load — lots of tiny kernels and CPU prefetch blocking. nvtx timeline shows repeated push/pop around KV lookup, then kernel selector thrashes. Uploading trace: https://internal-profiles/redwood/nsys/1832104567
ravi: Can you attach the trace here? Want to look at the kernel timeline.
jamie: https://internal-profiles/redwood/nsys/1832104567 (full nsys .qdrep + perfetto export)
profiler-bot: nsys upload complete: https://artifacts.redwood/trace/1832104567.qdrep :eyes:
sophie: Looks like the recent batching heuristic caused per-request selector on CPU. Selector runs -> small kernels launched per request -> lots of kernel switches and low occupancy.
maria: Ugh. We measured ~6% tail latency increase in canary after that change.
ravi: Do we have NVTX ranges for: kv.prefetch, kv.lookup, kernel.selector, kernel.launch? If not, add them. We need low-cardinality names.
jamie: There are ranges but name scheme included full request UUID which exploded series in perf dashboards.
sophie: Proposal for naming: use fixed component and step tags + numeric index. Example: "kv:prefetch/0", "kv:lookup/1", "selector:choose". Store request id in nvtxRangeId only (or as an attribute) not in the visible name.
maria: Agreed. For console correlation we can emit a separate per-request span (short name) and write the full id to logs/trace metadata. Don't use full uuid in nvtx string.
ravi: Also add a small cpu-side "kv.prefetch_cpu" range that wraps the memcpy/prefetch to see overlap with kernel.exec.
jamie: Quick sketch (C++) — avoid allocations in hot path:

```cpp
// pre-allocated char buf per-thread
thread_local char nvtx_buf[64];
int len = snprintf(nvtx_buf, sizeof(nvtx_buf), "kv:pf/%u", short_reqid);
nvtxRangePushA(nvtx_buf);
// ... work ...
nvtxRangePop();
```

Use nvtxRangePushA so we don't allocate.
sophie: For color/visualization, pick consistent colors for cpu-prefetch (blue), selector (orange), kernel.exec (green). Also set nvtxRangeId via nvtxRangeStartEx to carry numeric request id: this helps correlating without duplicating in name.
maria: On the profiling side, run nsys with `--trace=cuda,nvtx` and `--sample=none` for full timeline; for sampling runs use `--sample=cpu` to reduce size. Perfetto export is helpful for big traces.
jamie: Action items:
- add low-cardinality NVTX ranges: kv.prefetch_cpu, kv.lookup, selector.choose, kernel.launch (PR: jamie/eng-runtime/inst-1832)
- change naming to fixed tags + short numeric ids (work in progress)
- collect two traces: 30s full timeline + 5x sampling runs
- bisect batching change with and without selector by toggling selector via env

ravi: I can review the PR tomorrow :thumbsup:
